description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:563: `let path = alloc::vec![target.clone()];` — the only reason path[0] needs to be an owned Certificate is so it has the same type as the popped/pushed intermediates further down. The public API takes &Certificate, so the clone is necessarily allocated each call. Alternative: have PathCandidates hold the leaf as a separate &'a Certificate and the rest of path as Vec<Certificate>. Saves one Certificate clone (potentially KB of TBS bytes) per iterator. Modest win. The current shape is more uniform inside next() — the loop body treats path entries identically — and that uniformity is genuine value. Not worth churning unless profiling shows leaf clone as a hot allocation. Flag for awareness.
title: PathCandidates::new clones the target Certificate into path[0]
